title: Czech EET 2.0 for nail and beauty salons: what to do by 1 Jan 2027
lead: From 1 January 2027, businesses in Czechia must report every receipt to the tax office. With SalonGo you don't buy a till: switch EET on once and the app reports by itself.
v2: Businesses taking cash or card payments, including nail, hair, lash and beauty studios and chair renters with their own IČO.
v3: An EET certificate from the tax office's DIS+ portal, its password and your outlet number.
v4: Upload the certificate once. Every sale is then reported and the receipt prints with its FIK code.
v5: Included in every SalonGo plan, the Chair plan too. No extra fee.
s1d: Log in to the DIS+ tax portal, create an EET certificate for your outlet and download the file.
s2d: In EET settings, choose the file and enter its password and the outlet number. The app reads your name and IČO from the certificate.
s3d: Each receipt is reported the moment you take payment. The printed receipt carries the FIK code.
q1: Does SalonGo charge extra for EET?
a1: No. EET is included in every plan: Basic, Pro, Premium and Chair.
q2: I rent a chair in a salon and have my own IČO. How do I report EET?
a2: Use the Chair plan with your own EET certificate. Receipts are in your name and the salon owner can't see your revenue.
q3: What if I can't get the certificate myself?
a3: SalonGo support does it with you by phone or WhatsApp, in Czech or Vietnamese.
q4: Do I need a till or a special printer?
a4: No till. SalonGo runs on a computer, iPad or phone. For printed receipts, any 80 mm thermal printer works.
note: General information, not tax advice. For your salon's specific case, ask your accountant or the tax office.
cta: Try it and switch EET on
